newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian March net reserves rise to 6.6 trln rbls.
newsitem.headline: Russian March net reserves rise to 6.6 trln rbls.

text.p: Russia's net foreign currency reserves rose to 6.6 trillion roubles on March 1 from 3.2 trillion roubles on February 1, the central bank said.
Reserves were calculated at a rate of 5,560 roubles to the dollar, it said in its weekly bulletin.
The central bank issued the following data (trillions of roubles):
NOTE - data for March 1996 not available. 1996 reserves calculated at 4,640 roubles per dollar.

Net reserves exclude liabilities such as money borrowed from the International Monetary Fund and money invested by non-residents in government securities through the "S" account mechanism, which is to be repatriated. Thus, the total amount of reserves available to the central bank is higher than indicated.

Under Russia's $10 billion three-year loan from the International Monetary Fund, the Fund sets performance targets for the budget deficit, net domestic assets -- defined as the monetary base less net currency reserves -- and net reserves.
